newsitem.title: USA: Fruit beats estimates, off on price fears.
newsitem.headline: Fruit beats estimates, off on price fears.

text.p: Despite beating Wall Street's first-quarter earnings estimate by a penny, Fruit of the Loom Inc saw its shares tumble 4-1/8 to 33-3/8 Wednesday.
The company reported first-quarter net income of $0.28 per share, up from $0.16 per share in the same period last year. The First Call consensus was $0.27 per share in earnings.
"Everybody is a little perplexed. We came in line with pretty much everybody's expectations," said Mark Steinkrauss, spokesman for the Chicago-based apparel manufacturer.
"It's psychology and maybe some fast money," he said.
Analysts said the market was worried about wholesale T-shirt price cutting as manufacturers fight for market share.

"The whole group has been very weak ... There's substantial concern that there's some excess T-shirt product in the pipeline and there is some price-cutting," said LJR Redbook Research analyst Jay Meltzer.

Moreover, Meltzer said, negativity may be left from Russell Corp's report last week that first quarter net income was off from the year-ago level. "Since then the whole group has given up ground," Meltzer said.
On Fruit's decline, Prudential Securities industry analyst Jack Pickler said, "It's a bit of an over-reaction."

Price promotion on T-shirts has been going on for some time as manufacturers fight for market share, he said. "But there seems to be a little surprise on the part of some investors there's as much promotion going on," he said.
